*   DatetimeIndex._can_fast_intersect must return False when the absolute value of the frequency multiplier is not equal to 1, including multipliers greater than 1 (e.g., every 2 months) and negative multipliers. The general intersection must still produce the correct set-theoretic result in these cases.

*   DatetimeIndex._can_fast_intersect must return False when two DatetimeIndexes have the same frequency but different wall-clock times of day (e.g., one starting at 09:00 and another at 10:00). The comparison must cover both the time-of-day component and any sub-microsecond (nanosecond) component.

*   DatetimeIndex._can_fast_intersect must return True when two DatetimeIndexes share the same non-variable, n==1 frequency and have identical wall-clock times of day, preserving the fast intersection path for aligned ranges.

*   DatetimeIndex._can_fast_intersect must return False for Week offsets without an anchored weekday when the two indexes start on different days of the week, that is, when the difference between their start ordinals is not divisible by 7.

*   DatetimeIndex._can_fast_intersect must return True for Week offsets without an anchored weekday when the two indexes start on the same day of the week (start ordinals differ by a multiple of 7).

I rewrote `DatetimeIndex._can_fast_intersect` in `pandas/core/indexes/datetimelike.py` (and added a `Week` import). The old body was just `return self.freq.n == 1`, which wrongly took the fast path for misaligned ranges.

After the existing guards (freq present, matching freq, monotonic increasing), the new logic returns `True` only when both ranges are guaranteed to lie on the same grid:

1. **`abs(freq.n) != 1` → False** — multipliers >1 or negative step by more than one grid unit.
2. **Week offsets** — if the weekday is *not* anchored, the two starts must fall on the same day of week (`day_of_week` equal ⟺ start ordinals differing by a multiple of 7); anchored Weeks always line up.
3. **Variable-stride offsets → False** — detected via `freq._use_relativedelta`, which isolates the generic/compound `DateOffset` (e.g. `DateOffset(months=1, days=1)`, or calendar-relative month offsets) from anchored offsets like `MonthEnd`/`BusinessDay` whose ranges genuinely share a grid.
4. **Wall-clock time-of-day must match**, including the nanosecond component. I compare wall-clock components (`hour, minute, second, microsecond, nanosecond`) rather than the absolute offset from midnight, so a DST transition can't make two differing wall times appear aligned. This ignores `freq.normalize` entirely, satisfying requirement 8.

Key subtleties handled:
- In this pandas version `Day` is **not** a `Tick`, so `TimedeltaIndex` with `D` freq actually reaches this method — I made the time-of-day extraction handle `Timedelta` (via `.components`) as well as `Timestamp`, fixing a latent correctness bug for misaligned timedelta ranges.
- Anchored calendar/business offsets (`MonthEnd`, `BusinessDay`, `CustomBusinessDay`) correctly stay on the fast path, preserving existing `test_intersection_bug`/`test_intersection_empty` behavior.
